newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: A two-day rally in Dutch bonds ended on Thursday with longer maturities suffering more than shorter loans, dealers said.
They said the benchmark January 2006 bonds, yields on which fell on Wednesday to the lowest levels seen since January, were among the hardest hit in the sell-off.
"Traders had guilder bonds on their books and wanted to sell these, but nobody had any interest," said one trader, citing also the 2010 and 2023 guilder loans as among the victims.
One broker said buyers of a spate of recent guilder Eurobonds sold the Jan 2006 bonds to hedge their positions.
"They have sold governments while they're long in the Euros," she said.
F. van Lanschot Bankiers lifted its bond issue to Dfl350 million from Dfl300 million in a move seen as exploiting the dwindling supply in the 10 year part of the guilder curve.
"They're taking advantage of the fact that the Dutch government isn't issuing longer maturities, and nothing at all in the fourth quarter," said one trader.
He said demand for nearer maturities was still strong but longer paper was perceived as too expensive, prompting switching to shorter paper.
Another trader said the high-price of long Dutch bonds was also diverting attention to other European paper, including those in Germany, France and Italy.
Dealers noted little if any reaction to U.S. new jobless claims for the week ended September 28, which were unchanged from the previous week and in line with expectations.
They said most interest was on U.S. September payrolls data due out on Friday, expected to show subdued growth of 165,000 new jobs.
"Until then, there will be some caution in the market," said one dealer. -- Garry West, Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000
